concepts.proposed_markdown: Metronome's GTM reporting guide models a customer commit-burn curve by combining expected daily pacing from balance access schedules with actual consumption from finalized invoice line items and current-period draft line items. The model joins `line_item.commit_id` to the access-schedule balance ID, constrains consumption to the schedule service period, cumulatively sums attributed line-item totals, and leaves forecast heuristics to the merchant. Its SQL is explicitly generalized and includes unresolved aliases and table-name variants; production models must retain the dedicated Data Export table-grain, freshness, snapshot-selection, and duplicate-row rules. The guide's sample burn bands and outreach actions are operational heuristics rather than platform-enforced thresholds.
warnings: Do not describe the generalized SQL as executable or as an exact current schema contract.
Do not replace table-specific Data Export cadence, freshness, snapshot, or at-least-once rules with the guide's broad daily wording.
Treat the example burn-rate bands as merchant-selected playbook heuristics, not universal customer-health definitions.

concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-metronome-guides-reporting-insights-gtm-reporting-get-commit-and-usage-analytics]] — expected-versus-actual commit burn model, finalized and draft consumption inputs, export and SQL limitations, and GTM operational heuristics

A GTM analytics guide derives expected commit burn from an access schedule and actual burn from finalized plus current draft invoice line items. It joins a populated `line_item.commit_id` to the access-schedule balance ID and sums attributed line-item totals within that schedule's service period. A null commit ID cannot be attributed to a particular commit and is excluded from the curve. > [!warning] Contradiction
> The GTM guide labels every null commit ID as on-demand usage, while the revenue-reporting guide says null can mean on-demand or overage and requires client-defined metadata to distinguish them. Preserve only the non-attribution conclusion until classification is verified.
warnings: Do not generalize `commit_id IS NULL` to on-demand usage; existing revenue-reporting documentation also permits overage.
Do not imply that invoice-line aggregation alone captures every ledger event, expiration, correction, or true-up affecting a balance.
